title: Extract fields from documents · Level 3
slo: Distinguish basic OCR from schema-based document extraction.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe the Items field? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Items is a collection field. A collection holds multiple records.

options.text: It can hold multiple item records
options.rationale: Items can hold records for several ordered products. Each record can contain its own nested values.

options.text: It is one flat text value
options.error_type: Confuses a collection with flat text
options.rationale: Items is a collection, not one flat value. It holds multiple structured item records.
options.better_fit: Use this when a field holds one simple text value rather than several records.

feedback.intrinsic: Details for a bike, helmet, and shirt could be merged together and lose their connections.
feedback.instructional: A collection keeps multiple item records separate, with nested details for each one.

options.error_type: Confuses line items with invoice summary fields
options.rationale: Items holds the individual ordered products. Invoice total is a separate summary field for the final amount.
options.better_fit: Use this when the required value is the invoice's final amount due.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk could treat the list of products as if it were one final financial amount.
feedback.instructional: Items describes individual purchases; Invoice total summarizes the invoice amount.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Items is a collection that can hold multiple separate item records.

exercises.question_text: What does semantic field extraction use to map a value?

options.rationale: Semantic field extraction maps a value based on what it represents. It does not require one exact visible label.

options.error_type: Confuses semantic mapping with label matching
options.rationale: Semantic extraction can work when labels differ or are missing. It uses the value's meaning rather than exact label matching.
options.better_fit: Use this when a process requires one exact printed label and does not need meaning-based mapping.

feedback.intrinsic: An invoice marked Invoice # could be missed when the expected label is Invoice No.
feedback.instructional: Semantic extraction recognizes that different labels can represent the same invoice-number field.

options.rationale: Printed text order does not by itself establish meaning. Semantic extraction maps values to fields by what they represent.
options.better_fit: Use this when considering the visible order of words read from an image.

feedback.intrinsic: A number might be read in order but still be assigned to the wrong field.
feedback.instructional: Meaning-based mapping identifies the invoice-number concept, not just the order of printed words.

options.error_type: Confuses semantic mapping with flat extraction
options.rationale: Semantic mapping can place values in schema fields with defined structure. It is not limited to a flat text field.
options.better_fit: Use this when a required value is intentionally stored as one simple text field.

feedback.intrinsic: Important structured details could be treated as unconnected text.
feedback.instructional: Semantic extraction maps meaningful values to the fields defined by a schema.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Semantic field extraction maps values by their meaning, even when visible labels differ or are missing.

exercises.question_text: On an invoice, the field that holds several ordered products is the ___ collection.

parts.text: On an invoice, the field that holds several ordered products is the

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The individual products could be placed outside the field that keeps their separate details together.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose Items for several ordered products. It is the collection of line-item records.

exercises.explanation: Items is a collection because it holds multiple ordered-product records. Invoice total and Vendor name are single invoice fields, while OCR reads visible text.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The reason a changed label can still map to the intended field may become unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with semantic extraction, then state that it maps values by meaning to schema fields.

exercises.correct_answer: Semantic extraction maps values by meaning to schema fields
exercises.explanation: The sequence states the method, its action, the basis for that action, and where the value is placed. Meaning is what allows labels to differ or be absent.

exercises.question_text: Which fields can an invoice schema include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Vendor name is a common invoice schema field. It identifies the seller named on the invoice.
Invoice date is a common invoice schema field. It records the date associated with the invoice.
Shipping Charge is a listed invoice schema field. It represents the delivery amount.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with audio-call fields
options.rationale: A callback number is useful for a recorded-call schema. It is not listed as an invoice schema field.
options.better_fit: Use this when extracting key details from a voice message or recorded call.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker could capture phone details while missing financial invoice details.
feedback.instructional: Match the field to the content: callback numbers belong to calls, while invoices use fields such as shipping charge and total.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Vendor name, invoice date, and shipping charge are all fields an invoice schema can include.

options.text: Reads visible text from an image
options.rationale: Basic OCR reads printed text visible in images. It converts that text into editable and searchable digital text.
Basic OCR recognizes visible text but does not understand relationships between values. Structured fields can preserve relationships such as a price belonging to an item.
options.better_fit: Use this when schema-based extraction keeps related values together in structured fields.

feedback.intrinsic: A receipt could be readable, but its prices may not stay connected to the right products.
feedback.instructional: OCR reads text. Use structured fields when the relationship between values matters.

options.rationale: Basic OCR reads what is printed. Mapping a value by meaning is semantic field extraction.
options.better_fit: Use this when different labels, such as Invoice # and Invoice No., represent the same field.

feedback.intrinsic: A number may be read correctly but not be placed in the intended invoice field.
feedback.instructional: Meaning-based mapping goes beyond OCR; it identifies what a value represents.

options.rationale: A schema defines the fields to extract and their structure. OCR only reads visible text.
options.better_fit: Use this when deciding which invoice details, such as vendor name and total, must be captured.

feedback.intrinsic: The receipt words can be captured without identifying which business details are needed.
feedback.instructional: A schema defines required fields; OCR supplies readable text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Basic OCR reads visible printed text in an image and makes it usable as digital text.

exercises.question_text: An invoice schema uses a callback number as the invoice total.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A contact phone number could be mistaken for the amount a customer must pay.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Keep fields tied to their purpose: use Invoice total for the final amount and callback number for call follow-up.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Invoice total is a financial field, while a callback number belongs to a recorded-call schema.

exercises.question_text: Basic OCR understands the meaning and relationships between words.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The words may be readable, yet a price can still remain unlinked to its item.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Basic OCR extracts printed text only. Schema-based extraction handles meaningful fields and relationships.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Basic OCR recognizes visible text, but it does not understand meaning, context, or relationships.

exercises.question_text: What does a schema specify? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A schema describes the information that should be extracted. It lists the fields or entities that matter.
A schema also defines field structure. It can include nested and collection fields.

options.error_type: Confuses a schema with basic OCR
options.rationale: Reading visible printed words is basic OCR. A schema specifies meaningful fields and their structure.
options.better_fit: Use this for the text-reading part of processing scanned pages or receipt photos.

feedback.intrinsic: The needed vendor, total, and item structure would be left unspecified.
feedback.instructional: A schema is broader than visible words: it names the information to capture and its structure.

options.rationale: A schema describes information and structure, not a fixed page layout. Fields can be extracted even when labels differ or are missing.
options.better_fit: Use a layout description when you only need to describe where text appears on a page.

feedback.intrinsic: An invoice with changed labels could still contain the right details, but this choice would not describe those details.
feedback.instructional: Focus on the meaning and structure of required fields, not a fixed arrangement on a page.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A schema states both the information to extract and how that information is structured.

exercises.question_text: The technology that reads printed text from a scanned receipt is ___.

parts.text: The technology that reads printed text from a scanned receipt is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The receipt text would not be identified as readable digital text by that term.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose OCR for reading visible printed text. Schema-based extraction defines fields, while semantic extraction maps values by meaning.

exercises.explanation: OCR is the part that turns visible printed words in an image into editable, searchable digital text. Schema-based and semantic extraction add structure or meaning beyond text reading.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The field names may sound disconnected from the invoice structure that contains them.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the invoice schema, state that it can include fields, then name the fields.

exercises.correct_answer: An invoice schema can include vendor name and invoice total
exercises.explanation: The phrase starts with what is being described, then states its capability, followed by two fields it can contain. Vendor name and invoice total are both valid invoice fields.

options.text: A description of fields and structure
options.rationale: A schema describes the information to extract. It also defines how those fields are structured.

options.text: A tool that reads printed text
options.rationale: OCR reads printed text from images. A schema defines fields and structure.
options.better_fit: Use this for OCR when turning visible text into searchable digital text.

feedback.intrinsic: Printed words may be read, but the required business fields would not be defined.
feedback.instructional: Keep the roles separate: OCR reads text, while a schema describes the information to capture.

options.text: A number shown on an invoice
options.error_type: Confuses field definition with field value
options.rationale: An invoice number is a field value. A schema defines the InvoiceNumber field that can hold that value.
options.better_fit: Use this for a value found in the InvoiceNumber field.

feedback.intrinsic: A single invoice number would be captured without a clear description of what that number represents.
feedback.instructional: A schema is the planned field structure, not one value placed into it.

options.text: A visible label on a document
options.rationale: A visible label is wording printed on a page. A schema is the structured definition of the field, and labels can differ or be absent.
options.better_fit: Use this when referring to wording such as Invoice No. or Invoice #.

feedback.intrinsic: A field could be missed when its printed label changes or is absent.
feedback.instructional: A schema is not tied to one visible label; it describes the field to be extracted.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A schema is a description of the fields to extract and their structure.
